# Edit in Ableton Live

Everything goes through `voyager ableton` (JSON out, typed error codes), on macOS and
Windows. Never drive Live with keystrokes, clicks, AppleScript or by editing `.als` files.

## Connect

Run `voyager ableton doctor --json` and follow its `next`. On Windows `setup` installs
the control surface but cannot pick it in Live: relay its `next` (one setting) to the
user.

## The open set is the truth

The producer edits the same set while you work. Read it with
`voyager ableton state --json` before planning and after any failed edit; never reuse
names or values from earlier output. `state --track NAME --json` shows a track's device
parameters; add `--device NAME` for every parameter of one device. An `apply` sent
after the producer changed the set returns `ABLETON_SET_CHANGED` and applies nothing:
read again, keep their changes and rebuild the edit. Use `--force` only when the user
asked to replace their change.

## Edit

`voyager ableton apply --ops @ops.json --json` runs a batch as one undo step and
returns `changes`, the exact list of what changed; tell the user those by name. A
failing op rolls the batch back.

```json
[
  { "op": "device.load", "track": "Bass", "name": "Operator" },
  { "op": "track.set", "track": "Drums", "volume": "-4 dB", "sends": { "A": "-15 dB" } },
  { "op": "python", "code": "[d.name for d in song.tracks[1].devices]" }
]
```

- `python` runs in Live against its Object Model with `song`, `app` and `Live`, and
  returns printed output and the last expression's value. Keep each op under 5 s.
- `track.set` sets a fader and sends in dB. `device.load` loads a Live device by name,
  or a preset, kit or sample by the `uri` from `voyager ableton browse QUERY --json`.
- Live's API won't automate arrangement clips: put the envelope on the session clip,
  then copy it to the arrangement (`track.duplicate_clip_to_arrangement`). The copy
  keeps the envelope, though the API reads it back as `None`.
- Nothing saves the set; tell the user to save in Live.

## Bounce and listen

`voyager ableton bounce --output /absolute/new.wav --json` renders the Arrangement
(`--start`, `--length` for a section, `--stems` for one WAV per track). The reply gives
`integratedLufs` and `truePeakDbtp`; fix loudness in the set, not the file. You cannot
hear: report measurements, never that it sounds good.

Bounce is macOS-only. On Windows ask the user to export in Live (File → Export
Audio/Video, WAV) and give you the file path, then analyse that file ([make-music](../make-music/SKILL.md#critique-a-track-or-mix)).
